newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia says could boost oil flow to Germany, Polan.
newsitem.headline: Russia says could boost oil flow to Germany, Polan.

text.p: Russia's oil pipeline monopoly Transneft said on Thursday it could boost crude oil supplies to Germany and Poland by nearly half to 50 million tonnes a year (one million barrels a day, or bpd) by 2000.

Transneft Vice-President Sergei Ter-Sarkisyants was quoted by Interfax news agency as saying the under-utilised Druzhba, or Friendship, pipeline linking Russia to Europe could carry an additional 20 million tonnes a year (400,000 bpd).
He did not say whether Russia planned to increase deliveries to Eastern and Central Europe or was merely capable of doing so.

But Sarkisyants said Transneft had been in preliminary talks with Elf-Aquitaine on the matter, since the French oil company had a 76 percent stake in a new oil refinery project in Leuna, Germany. The refinery aims to secure 10 million tonnes (200,000 bpd) of Russian oil a year through Druzhba.
He also said Transneft could increase supplies to Slovenia, Croatia and Serbia via Druzhba and the Adria pipeline without investing in any capital improvements.

Druzhba, which has two trunk sections, one through Ukraine and one through Belarus, has been working far below capacity since the Soviet Union fell apart in 1991 and customers diversified supplies. It operated at less than one third of its capacity last year, carrying only 16.6 million tonnes (326,000 bpd).
In the first quarter, Russia used the link to deliver 247,000 bpd to Germany, 214,000 bpd to Poland, 94,400 bpd to the Czech Republic and 93,300 bpd to Slovakia.
